input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 imposes the MFN on us, not on Vendor: we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit and no comparability carve-outs. That is the rule's walk-away case (open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor) and falls well short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is affected; the minimal fix is deletion of § 7.2, reaching the preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the requirement that we disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit: our playbook does not accept MFN obligations running against us, and this open-ended matching right also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have given no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
proposal.summary: Delete the MFN/right-to-match obligation imposed on Customer in § 7.2.
